grf.generated_reality: A CM-TERM PROCESS_DIRECT effect that merely promises no shell is still underspecified: command-name PATH lookup and exact/pinned executable identity are materially different host semantics.
grf.counter_reality: Direct exec-family launch by command name may appear equivalent to launching an expected executable path in benign environments, while a changed PATH can select a different executable without any shell being involved.
grf.discriminator: With a temporary executable named printf placed first in PATH, compare Linux execve on the explicit /usr/bin/printf pathname against execvp on the bare name printf.
grf.outcome: RETAIN the distinction. No-implicit-shell is necessary but insufficient to define executable identity.

unusual_experiment.setup: Built a disposable executable named printf that prints SHADOW_EXECUTED and prepended its temporary directory to PATH.

baseline.mechanism: execve('/usr/bin/printf', argv, envp) with the hostile PATH still present in envp

unusual_experiment.result: The direct name-based exec path selected the PATH shadow while the explicit pathname selected /usr/bin/printf. Both paths avoided an implicit shell.
unusual_experiment.rollback: The shadow executable and temporary directory were deleted; the explicit rollback check observed shadow_removed=true.
unusual_experiment.external_effects: Disposable local/container process and filesystem only; no product repository mutation, VPS mutation, network/provider effect, Clay authority, training or canonical runtime state mutation.

primary_evidence.finding: execvp/execlp search PATH when the file argument contains no slash; pathname-taking exec variants do not perform that search.
execve executes the program referred to by the supplied path and directly supplies argv/envp.
execvp performs PATH-based pathname construction for a file name without slash; fexecve identifies the executable by file descriptor.

fexecve executes the file referred to by an fd and is explicitly motivated by avoiding pathname replacement between integrity checking and execution; mutable-file permissions remain a separate caveat.
execveat with AT_EMPTY_PATH can execute the file referred to by a file descriptor and provides a Linux-specific object-bound candidate surface.

proposal: Keep PROCESS_DIRECT, SHELL_EXPLICIT and PTY_INTERACTIVE separate as already supported by the concurrent CM-TERM shell-boundary receipt.
Within PROCESS_DIRECT, make executable resolution mode Clay-visible rather than implicit: at minimum distinguish EXACT_PATH from PATH_SEARCH; unknown mode fails closed.
A PATH_SEARCH request must receipt-bind the requested name, effective PATH/search inputs and the actually resolved executable identity before claiming the observed outcome belongs to that command.

For security-/release-sensitive launches, evaluate an FD_PINNED mode based on fexecve or execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH) so integrity observation and execution can refer to the same opened object; this is a candidate, not yet selected semantics.
Do not claim that an executable digest alone solves mutability/TOCTOU; permissions/object mutability and interpreter-script behavior require their own tests.
Canonical CM-TERM regression should include a PATH-shadow case and require deterministic distinction between exact/pinned and search-based modes.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: A portable Clay Environment may intentionally rely on PATH search for ordinary user commands, and forbidding it would reduce usability. The proposed contract therefore does not ban PATH search; it makes it explicit, observable and separately authorizable.
architecture_delta.promotion_gate: No CM-TERM implementation PASS from this receipt. Promotion requires the canonical ClayCode -> typed/effect IR -> ClayVM -> Clay Environment path to exercise the selected modes on real Linux, with streaming I/O, exit/failure/cancellation semantics and receipts.
